defects.acceptance_condition: Retain the advertised finite low-value partition and Theorem 2.3 alpha-envy endpoint, while making the constructive high-atom/residual partition route explicit and independent of the non-progressing printed choice.
defects.repair_obligation: A progressing partition construction must choose a maximal or supremal feasible endpoint (with the required measurable limiting argument), not a minimum feasible endpoint: x = 0 is feasible and cannot advance the cut.
defects.resolution_evidence: `Lemma24.theorem2_3_real_interval_supported_atom_bound` splits the finite aggregate high-point set, invokes a finite residual real-interval partition at alpha/2, and applies the finite allocation theorem. Its progress is supplied by the partition certificate and does not use the printed minimum-endpoint instruction.
defects.source_claim: Lemma 2.4 claims a finite partition of [0,1] into pieces of value at most alpha for every player. Its proof says to choose the minimum x whose prefix [0,x] has value at most alpha for every player.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The error is confined to an auxiliary proof step. The repaired Lean route establishes the same advertised alpha-bounded allocation result, so it is a disclosed formalization note rather than a caveat or a change to the mathematical endpoint.
